prompt.context_jp: 経理部の給湯室に、朝から不穏な噂が漂っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 経理部の給湯室に、朝から不穏な噂___漂っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits this opening-scene description.

feedback.correct_en: This is the opening sentence introducing a brand-new element — the rumor — into the scene. New-information subjects of existence/appearance verbs like 漂う take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would wrongly treat 'the rumor' as a known topic the reader already has in mind. を doesn't fit an intransitive verb like 漂う.

contrast_examples.en: There was a man in the room. (new info)

prompt.context_jp: 沙名子はカップを手にしたまま、同僚たちの声にじっと耳を傾けていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 沙名子___カップを手にしたまま、同僚たちの声にじっと耳を傾けていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits here, where Sanako is the established protagonist being described?

feedback.correct_en: Sanako is the known protagonist and the sentence describes what she as topic was doing. は marks her as the running theme of the narration.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present her as new information, which clashes with her being the familiar main character. に is a location/direction particle and doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.jp: そのとき沙名子が入ってきた。
contrast_examples.en: Just then Sanako came in. (new appearance)

prompt.context_jp: 「森若さんが言ったんですよね？ メールのこと」
prompt.prompt_jp: 森若さん___言ったんですよね？
prompt.prompt_en: Arimoto is identifying exactly who told the manager. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Arimoto is pinning down which specific person spilled the secret — an exhaustive-listing/identification use of が ('it was Moriwaka who told you, right?').
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'Moriwaka' a mere topic and lose the pointed accusation. を doesn't fit a subject role.

contrast_examples.en: It's Moriwaka who is the culprit. (identification)
As for Moriwaka, she's in accounting. (topic)

prompt.context_jp: 「昨日 有本さんが提出した注文書は 恐らく偽物です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 昨日 有本さんが提出した注文書___ 恐らく偽物です。
prompt.prompt_en: Sanako is making a judgment about a specific, already-mentioned document. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: The purchase order is the known topic under discussion; は sets it up as 'as for that order…' and leads to the predicate '偽物です'.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly introduce the order as brand-new information, when it has just been under scrutiny. に doesn't fit the subject slot.

contrast_examples.en: This document is a fake. (judgment about a known topic)
There is a fake document. (presenting new info)

prompt.context_jp: 「問題は そのこと自体ではなく それを指摘したときの 有本さんの動揺です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 問題___ そのこと自体ではなく、有本さんの動揺です。
prompt.prompt_en: Sanako is contrasting what the problem is NOT vs what it IS. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: '問題は' sets up 'the problem' as the topic she's about to characterize, then contrasts 'not X, but Y'. は is standard for this kind of definitional, contrastive framing.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present '問題' as new info in a listing sense, which clashes with the explanatory 'A ではなく B' structure. も (also) doesn't fit the exclusive contrast.

contrast_examples.jp: 大事なのは結果ではなく過程だ。
contrast_examples.en: What matters is not the result but the process.

prompt.context_jp: 「よく気付きましたね 新島部長」 「私___ お伝えしました」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___ お伝えしました。
prompt.prompt_en: Sanako corrects the credit: it was she herself (not Niijima) who noticed. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: She's identifying the actual agent — 'It was I who informed him.' This exhaustive/identificational use takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: '私は' would read as a mild topic shift ('as for me, I informed him'), weaker than the correcting-the-record force needed. で doesn't fit a subject.

contrast_examples.en: I'm the one who did it.
I did it (among other things/as for me).

prompt.context_jp: 山田太陽が経理部に姿を見せると、フロアの空気がわずかに緩んだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 山田太陽___経理部に姿を見せると、フロアの空気がわずかに緩んだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this subordinate clause describing an event happening?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a 〜と subordinate clause reporting a fresh event, the subject typically takes が. Yamada's appearance is new information triggering the main clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: は can't normally mark the subject inside a 〜と temporal/conditional clause like this. を doesn't fit an intransitive verb.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が来ると、皆が笑った。

contrast_examples.en: He said he wouldn't come. (main-clause topic)

prompt.context_jp: 周囲の視線を意識しているのは、どうやら沙名子ひとりのようだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 周囲の視線を意識しているのは、どうやら沙名子ひとり___ようだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill the particle after '沙名子ひとり' in this cleft-like sentence.

feedback.correct_en: The structure is '〜のは…のようだ' — the predicate noun before ようだ takes の to connect: 'the one who X seems to be only Sanako.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would be ungrammatical before ようだ in this nominal predicate. を doesn't fit at all.

contrast_examples.en: The one who came seems to be him.

prompt.context_jp: 沙名子だけが、そのそっけない背中を目で追っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 沙名子だけ___ そのそっけない背中を目で追っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle completes 'only Sanako was following…'?

feedback.correct_en: '〜だけが' identifies Sanako as the sole person doing the action — a prototypical exhaustive-listing use of が.
feedback.incorrect_en: '〜だけは' would shift to contrastive topic ('at least only Sanako…'), which doesn't match the narrator's identifying tone. に doesn't fit a subject.

prompt.context_jp: 誰かが小さく息を呑む音が、静まりかえった経理部にはっきりと響いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 誰か___ 小さく息を呑む音が、静まりかえった経理部にはっきりと響いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits with 誰か as the subject of the inner clause?

feedback.correct_en: Indefinite subjects like 誰か ('someone') are inherently new/non-specific and must take が, not は.
feedback.incorrect_en: '誰かは' is odd because は presupposes a known referent, which 誰か doesn't give. を doesn't fit a subject.

prompt.context_jp: 「森若さん 私のことだったら もう…」 「あなたのためじゃありません」
prompt.prompt_jp: あなたのため___ ありません。
prompt.prompt_en: Sanako denies that her stand is for Mabuki's sake, implicitly contrasting with another reason. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: 'じゃありません' (= ではありません) negates the predicate 'for your sake', with the implicit contrast 'but for another reason'. The は inside では is doing the contrastive work.
feedback.incorrect_en: 'が ありません' would mean 'there is no X for you', a possession sense that doesn't fit. を doesn't fit a copular predicate.

contrast_examples.en: It's not for your sake (but for something else).

prompt.context_jp: 沙名子の声は、抑えているぶんだけ余計に鋭く響いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 沙名子の声___ 抑えているぶんだけ余計に鋭く響いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for 'Sanako's voice' as the topic being characterized?

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is describing a property of Sanako's voice in a reflective, topic-comment way. は sets up 'as for her voice…' and leads to a general observation.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it a one-time new event, but this is a general evaluative statement about the quality of her voice. で doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.en: At that moment, a voice was heard. (event)

prompt.context_jp: 沈黙を破ったのは、意外にも田倉だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 沈黙を破ったの___ 意外にも田倉だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this cleft sentence identifying who broke the silence?

feedback.correct_en: In a cleft '〜のは…だ' structure, the nominalized clause is topicalized with は, and the identified referent follows. 'The one who broke the silence was Takakura.'
feedback.incorrect_en: '〜のが' would make it the subject of a larger predicate, not a cleft identification. を doesn't fit here.

contrast_examples.en: The one who came is Tanaka.

prompt.context_jp: 有本の顔から、笑みという笑みが剥がれ落ちていく。
prompt.prompt_jp: 有本の顔から、笑みという笑み___ 剥がれ落ちていく。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the subject '笑みという笑み' (every last smile)?

feedback.correct_en: '〜という〜' emphasizes the whole set as a vivid new event unfolding — the smiles peeling away. Narrative event descriptions of this kind take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn it into a general topic statement, losing the sense of a scene playing out in real time. に doesn't fit a subject.

prompt.context_jp: 「お中元の送り状を 丁寧に手書きで書かれる方が あんな大切な内容を メールで送るかなと」
prompt.prompt_jp: お中元の送り状___ 丁寧に手書きで書かれる方が…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the invoice as the direct object of 書く here?

feedback.correct_en: 送り状 is the thing being written — the direct object of 書く. を is the standard direct-object marker.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would read 'the invoice writes…' which is nonsensical. は would topicalize it in a way that fights the embedded relative-clause structure.

prompt.context_jp: 「同じ万年筆で 書かれています」
prompt.prompt_jp: 同じ万年筆___ 書かれています。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the fountain pen as the instrument used?

feedback.correct_en: で marks the means/instrument — written with the same fountain pen.
feedback.incorrect_en: に marks location/direction, not the tool. を would read as the direct object, but the pen is the instrument, not what's being written.

prompt.context_jp: 「証拠はあります みかど旅館から ファックスで送っていただきました」
prompt.prompt_jp: みかど旅館から ファックス___ 送っていただきました。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the fax as the medium of sending?

feedback.correct_en: で marks fax as the means of transmission — 'sent to us by fax.'
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark a destination, not a means. が doesn't fit this adverbial slot.

prompt.context_jp: 「本物の注文書は 半年前 みかど旅館から 受け取った直後に ___しまったからでしょうね」
prompt.prompt_jp: 受け取った直後に ___ しまったからでしょうね。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits: she destroyed the real purchase order right after receiving it?

feedback.correct_en: 処分する means to dispose of / get rid of — the exact action of destroying evidence here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 処理する is broader 'to process/handle' and doesn't specifically mean destroy. 処方する is for prescribing medicine.

prompt.context_jp: 「取り引きをなかったことにして 現金で受け取った売上金を ___するため」
prompt.prompt_jp: 現金で受け取った売上金を ___ するため。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word means to embezzle / pocket the cash?

feedback.correct_en: 着服 (chakufuku) specifically means to misappropriate / embezzle money — the exact crime being described.
feedback.incorrect_en: 着任 = taking a post; 着目 = focusing attention on. Neither has anything to do with pocketing money.

contrast_examples.jp: 新しいポストに着任する。

prompt.context_jp: 「麻吹さんから いわれのない ___ を受けて 精神的なダメージを負ったと 訴えたそうです」
prompt.prompt_jp: いわれのない ___ を受けて…
prompt.prompt_en: Which word means 'defamation / slander' here?

feedback.correct_en: 誹謗中傷 is the standard four-character compound for 'slander and defamation', matching Arimoto's accusation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 一期一会 (a once-in-a-lifetime encounter) and 起承転結 (structure of a story) are unrelated idioms.

prompt.context_jp: 「みかど旅館のご主人からのメールは あなたが ___ 打った 自作自演なのではと」
prompt.prompt_jp: あなたが ___ 打った自作自演なのではと。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word means 'impersonating / pretending to be someone else'?

feedback.correct_en: 成り済ます means to pass oneself off as someone else — Sanako is accusing her of impersonating the inn owner.
feedback.incorrect_en: 成り立つ = 'to be established/to hold true'. 成り行き = 'course of events'. Neither captures impersonation.

prompt.context_jp: 不正を美談で覆えば、そこには必ず次の不正が ___ 。
prompt.prompt_jp: 次の不正が ___ 。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits: 'the next wrongdoing will take root'?

feedback.correct_en: 根を張る literally means 'to spread roots' — a vivid metaphor for wrongdoing becoming entrenched.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手を打つ = 'to take action/measures'. 首を切る = 'to fire someone'. Neither matches the image of entrenchment.

prompt.context_jp: 有本の口元は、 ___ 笑みを隠そうともしなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: ___ 笑みを隠そうともしなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word best fits 'a triumphant smile'?

feedback.correct_en: 勝ち誇った = 'triumphant', matching Arimoto's gloating smile after beating Mabuki's accusation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 恥じらった = 'bashful'. うなだれた = 'with head hung low'. Both are the opposite feel.

prompt.context_jp: 消えたメールの復元というやや ___ の依頼にも、彼はいつもの調子で快く応じてくれる。
prompt.prompt_jp: やや ___ の依頼にも、彼は快く応じてくれる。
prompt.prompt_en: Which expression means 'outside one's area of expertise'?

feedback.correct_en: 畑違い literally 'different field (lit. farm)' — perfect for 'somewhat outside his specialty' (asking a salesman to recover emails).
feedback.incorrect_en: 筋違い implies an unreasonable/misdirected request. 見当違い means 'wide of the mark'. Neither captures the specialty-mismatch nuance.

prompt.context_jp: 「受けた恩には 最高の礼をもって ___ です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 受けた恩には 最高の礼をもって ___ です。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb best completes 'one should repay kindness with the utmost courtesy'?

feedback.correct_en: 恩に報いる is a set phrase meaning 'to repay a kindness/debt of gratitude'. It fits Arimoto's self-serving speech about repaying debts.
feedback.incorrect_en: 逃れる = 'to escape', 恐れる = 'to fear'; neither forms a natural collocation with 恩.

prompt.context_jp: Opening line: an unsettling rumor has been drifting around since morning.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural as the opening sentence of this chapter?

choices.text: 経理部の給湯室に、朝から不穏な噂が漂っていた。
経理部の給湯室に、朝から不穏な噂は漂っていた。

feedback.correct_en: An opening narrative sentence introducing a new element — the rumor — into the scene naturally takes が. The reader is meeting the rumor for the first time.
feedback.incorrect_en: '噂は' would imply the rumor is already a known topic being commented on, which doesn't fit as the opening line of the chapter.

contrast_examples.en: There was a cat in the garden. (new info)

prompt.context_jp: Mabuki apologizes to the president and executives in a formal reception room.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds right for Mabuki's humble, formal apology to top executives?

choices.text: 私が間違っておりました。

feedback.correct_en: 〜ておりました is the humble form of 〜ていました, appropriate when addressing company executives in a formal setting.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜てたよ is casual spoken form; wildly inappropriate for an apology to the president and board.

prompt.context_jp: Sanako firmly reframes the confrontation as official accounting business, not a detective game.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural for Sanako's measured, professional pushback?

choices.text: 経理部として 有本さんの不正について お話ししています。
経理部として 有本さんの不正について 話してるんだけど。

feedback.correct_en: お話ししています uses humble お〜する + polite ます, matching Sanako's controlled, by-the-book professional stance.
feedback.incorrect_en: 話してるんだけど is colloquial and softens into a complaint, undercutting the official 'as the accounting department' framing.

prompt.context_jp: The others look away, but Sanako alone keeps her eyes on Yamada's retreating back.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for 'only Sanako was watching his back'?

choices.text: 沙名子だけが、そのそっけない背中を目で追っていた。
沙名子だけは、そのそっけない背中を目で追っていた。

feedback.correct_en: 〜だけが identifies Sanako as the exclusive doer in a plain narrative description — the exhaustive-listing use of が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜だけは would push a contrastive 'at least Sanako…' nuance, which doesn't fit this quiet observation about the scene.

contrast_examples.en: She alone remained (contrast with others leaving).

prompt.context_jp: Yamada softly calls after Sanako: don't rush, let's take our time.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version matches Yamada's gentle, intimate tone with Sanako?

choices.text: ゆっくり参りましょう。

feedback.correct_en: The volitional 〜いこう (casual 'let's go') captures Yamada's warm, close register. He's speaking personally, not formally.
feedback.incorrect_en: 参りましょう is a humble/business level that would feel distant and stiff in a tender personal moment.

contrast_examples.jp: ご一緒いたしましょう。
contrast_examples.en: Allow me to accompany you. (very formal)
